description: Cuts out part of a plan, so that you can send a smaller plan when your context is short: the scenes, the shots or the sequence you name, with everything they refer to (characters, places, props, sound and the rest) and their times unchanged. The slice is a valid plan of its own, so you can send it to shoot_plan_check, and it says which whole plan it was cut from (slice_of). It is for reading and editing one part: to change the film, change the whole plan and check that. Input: plan, and exactly one of scenes (scene ids), shots (shot ids) or sequence (one sequence id). Ids may be a name, a comma-separated list, or a list of names. An id the plan does not have is refused, and the refusal says what to change. Output: the sliced dpl.plan/1 with slice_of. A slice of shots that leaves gaps in a scene is judged as if the shots on either side of a gap were neighbours: treat its check as advice. No AI model runs. We don't keep the plan. We log a one-way fingerprint (hash) of it, its size, the tool, the type of client, the result and the time taken. Needs an agent key from a Shoot Plan account. Free, and it does not count toward the account's 3 free projects a month. Plans up to 8 MB and 120 calls a minute (5,000 a day).

plan.description: The plan itself: a dpl.plan/1 JSON object (not text inside a string). Call shoot_plan_format for the schema links and an example.

scenes.description: Slice these scenes: scene ids (a name, a comma-separated list, or a list of names).

sequence.description: Slice this one sequence: a sequence id.

shots.description: Slice these shots: shot ids (a name, a comma-separated list, or a list of names).

name: shoot_plan_slice
title: Cut a smaller plan out of a big one
